workstream: Wave 3C-1b — Current Makati public health-facility verification
scope: Research/reconciliation only. No Civic Map health-center assets are added in this step.

controllingCounts.source: Makati City Basic Facts and Figures 2023
controllingCounts.note: The 2023 city statistic is retained as the MHD-network denominator. Newer evidence is used to identify the current named sites.

methodology: Use the 2026 PhilHealth YAKAP list as strongest current operating evidence where a Makati city health center appears with a current address.
Use 2026 PhilHealth TB DOTS accreditation and the current DOH NTP directory to fill current MHD-network sites absent from YAKAP.
Use older Makati Health Department directories only for historical continuity and alias/address comparison.
Do not count the Makati Health Department employee clinic at City Hall as one of the 18 barangay/community health centers.
Treat barangay-run or supplementary public clinics separately from the MHD 18 unless a city source explicitly places them in that denominator.
Do not create a second Civic Map pin for a service designation operating at the same physical health-center site.

reconciliationFindings: The 18-center 2023 headline can be matched to 18 currently evidenced MHD-network sites without using the City Hall employee clinic.
Sixteen of the 18 are directly listed in the May 31, 2026 PhilHealth YAKAP roster.
San Antonio is separately current in PhilHealth's May 31, 2026 TB DOTS roster.
Valenzuela remains a current City of Makati public Rural Health Unit/Health Center in the DOH National TB Control Program directory.
Both Pio PC and Pio RHU remain current, so they must stay as separate physical sites.
Palanan's 24/7 designation is co-located with Palanan Health Center and should not become a duplicate pin.

San Lorenzo has current public medical/dental clinic sites, but the reviewed evidence does not place them inside the official MHD 18-center denominator; keep them as a separate public-clinic layer pending implementation scope.
